idea.title: Verify a Pages project name independently from its hostname
idea.summary: A read-only release audit found that Pages project names differed from their existing pages.dev hostnames and from the names used in release tooling.

context.goal: Verify Pages project identities and automatic deployment settings before a staging rehearsal.
context.situation: Two Git-integrated Pages projects retained older pages.dev hostnames after their project names differed from those hostnames.
context.investigation: The Cloudflare API project list and individual project records returned the current names, hostnames, Git branches, and automatic deployment settings. Lookups using the hostname prefixes returned project-not-found errors. The release commands and their preflight checks used the older names.
context.result: Both release targets need correction. The staging API record still reported automatic production-branch deployments enabled and all preview branches enabled, despite a reported dashboard change. No deployment or configuration change was performed.

learning_points: Identify cloud resources by the API project name rather than deriving it from a hostname.
Check production and preview branch deployment controls separately and re-read the live state.
Include identity preflight checks and their tests when correcting release tooling.
possible_angles: Resource identity can differ from the URL that users see.
A read-only release audit can reveal mismatched targets and deployment settings before a rehearsal.
